Title: Mitigating Traffic Oscillations in Mixed Traffic Flow with Scalable Deep Koopman Predictive Control - ADS
## ADS. ## Mitigating Traffic Oscillations in Mixed Traffic Flow with Scalable Deep Koopman Predictive Control. #### Abstract. Mitigating traffic oscillations in mixed flows of connected automated vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs) is critical for enhancing traffic stability. A key challenge lies in modeling the nonlinear, heterogeneous behaviors of HDVs within computationally tractable predictive control frameworks. This study proposes an adaptive deep Koopman predictive control framework (AdapKoopPC) to address this issue. The framework features a novel deep Koopman network, AdapKoopnet, which represents complex HDV car-following dynamics as a linear system in a high-dimensional space by adaptively learning from naturalistic data. This learned linear representation is then embedded into a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, enabling real-time, scalable, and optimal control of CAVs. We validate our framework using the HighD dataset and extensive numerical simulations. Results demonstrate that AdapKoopnet achieves superior trajectory prediction accuracy over baseline models. Furthermore, the complete AdapKoopPC controller significantly dampens traffic oscillations with lower computational cost, exhibiting strong performance even at low CAV penetration rates. The proposed framework offers a scalable and data-driven solution for enhancing stability in realistic mixed traffic environments. The code is made publicly available. :   10.48550/arXiv.2502.00043. :   Advanced Engineering Informatics, Vol. 71, Part A, 104258, 2026.

This paper proposes a decentralized robust DeeP-LCC (Data-EnablEd Predictive Leading Cruise Control) approach for CAVs to smooth mixed traffic, which greatly reduces computation complexity with better safety performance, while naturally preserving data privacy. ### DeeP-LCC: Data-EnablEd Predictive Leading Cruise Control in Mixed Traffic Flow. This article introduces a data-driven nonparametric strategy, called Data-EnablEd Predictive Leading Cruise Control (DeeP-LCC), to achieve safe and optimal control of CAVs in mixed traffic and demonstrates its great potential on improving traffic efficiency, driving safety, and fuel economy. ### Robust Platoon Control in Mixed Traffic Flow Based on Tube Model Predictive Control. ### Robust Nonlinear Data-Driven Predictive Control for Mixed Vehicle Platoons via Koopman Operator and Reachability Analysis. A Robust Nonlinear Data-Driven Predictive Control (RNDDPC) framework that ensures safe and optimal control under uncertain and adverse conditions is proposed and significantly outperforms baseline methods in tracking performance under noise, disturbances, and attacks. ### Uncertainty-Aware Dynamics Modeling and Data-Driven Robust Predictive Control for Mixed Vehicle Platoon. The results show that DVKoN can accurately predict the uncertain car-following behavior of HDVs in the mixed vehicle platoon and the proposed DVKoRPC can effectively alleviate traffic oscillations, improve traffic efficiency, and reduce fuel consumption. ### A Predictive Deep-Reinforcement-Learning-Based Connected Automated Vehicle Anticipatory Longitudinal Control in a Mixed Traffic Lane Change Condition. ### Robust Explicit Data-Driven Predictive Control for Mixed Vehicle Platoons. A robust explicit data-driven predictive control (REDDPC) framework designed to provide robust and real-time control for mixed vehicle platoons is proposed, achieving superior tracking performance under noise, disturbance, and attack conditions, while significantly reducing online computational time, making it highly suitable for real-world deployment.

results.content: # Full length article Mitigating traffic oscillations in mixed traffic flow with scalable deep Koopman predictive control. This learned linear representation is then embedded into a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, enabling real-time, scalable, and optimal control of CAVs. We validate our framework using the HighD dataset and extensive numerical simulations. While advanced data-driven models, such as those based on deep learning, have demonstrated superior accuracy in capturing these complex dynamics [16], their non-convex and computationally intensive nature makes them ill-suited for direct integration into real-time optimization frameworks [17], [18]. This creates a dilemma: high-fidelity nonlinear prediction models compromise real-time control feasibility, whereas overly simplified models fail to capture essential traffic dynamics, leading to suboptimal or unsafe CAV actions [22], [23]. To resolve this prediction-control dilemma, this paper introduces the Koopman operator theory as a powerful mathematical framework to model and predict nonlinear HDV dynamics in a manner that is amenable to real-time predictive control. This framework is designed to learn heterogeneous HDV behaviors from naturalistic driving data and deploy scalable, real-time control strategies for CAVs to mitigate traffic oscillations. We propose **AdapKoopPC**, a scalable predictive control framework embedding AdapKoopnet’s linear representations into MPC for real-time, cooperative CAV control in arbitrary mixed traffic configurations. ## Car-following behavior modeling and prediction of HDVs. Accurate prediction of HDVs behavior is a critical prerequisite for the effective control of CAVs in mixed traffic. The core idea is to first accurately predict the complex, nonlinear behavior of HDVs and then embed this high-fidelity predictive model into a computationally tractable MPC scheme to optimally control the CAVs. Our approach first defines the local mixed traffic system we aim to control. ## AdapKoopnet: Adaptive deep Koopman network for car following behavior modeling and prediction of HDVs. In this section, a data-driven adaptive deep Koopman linear model is proposed to address the challenges associated with real-time cognition and prediction of the state of HDVs. This study addressed the fundamental challenge of mitigating traffic oscillations in mixed traffic flow: the inherent conflict between the need for high-fidelity, nonlinear models of HDV behavior and the requirement for computationally tractable, linear models for real-time MPC.
